title: Predict the changing list
idea: Pure tracing: follow a list through a mix of append and item-assignment steps. Thinking-heavy, reinforces how each step reshapes the list.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [1, 2]
n.append(3)
n[0] = 9
print(n)
exercises.explanation: append 3 gives [1, 2, 3]; then n[0] = 9 changes the first spot: [9, 2, 3]. Trace one step at a time.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = []
n.append(4)
n.append(5)
n[0] = 40
print(n)
exercises.explanation: Appends build [4, 5]; then n[0] = 40 replaces the first item: [40, 5].

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [10, 20, 30]
n[1] = 0
n.append(40)
print(n)
exercises.explanation: n[1] = 0 gives [10, 0, 30]; append 40 adds to the end: [10, 0, 30, 40].

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [5]
n.append(5)
n.append(5)
n[0] = 1
print(n)
exercises.explanation: Appends build [5, 5, 5]; then n[0] = 1 changes only the first: [1, 5, 5].

exercises.prompt:
This should end as [2, 2]. Fill the missing step:

n = [1]
n.append(2)
n[0] = ____
print(n)
exercises.explanation: After append, n is [1, 2]. Setting n[0] = 2 makes it [2, 2].

exercises.prompt: Predict: after n = [1, 2]; n.append(3), the list n has 3 items.
exercises.explanation: append added one item, so the count went from 2 to 3. The list is now [1, 2, 3].

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [1, 2, 3]
n[-1] = 99
print(n)
exercises.explanation: n[-1] is the last spot, so assigning 99 there gives [1, 2, 99]. Negative positions work for assignment too.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [0, 0, 0]
n[1] = 5
n.append(5)
print(n)
exercises.explanation: n[1] = 5 gives [0, 5, 0]; append 5 adds to the end: [0, 5, 0, 5].

exercises.prompt: These steps turn [1, 2] into [1, 2, 3] then into [1, 9, 3]. Put them in the order that produces that result.
exercises.explanation: Start [1, 2], append 3 -> [1, 2, 3], then n[1] = 9 -> [1, 9, 3]. Order of steps matters.

exercises.prompt: Which single step GROWS the list, and which only CHANGES it?
exercises.explanation: append adds a new item (longer list); list[i] = value swaps an existing item (same length). Keep that pair straight.
